question: Is buying work injury compensation (WIC) insurance mandatory for Employment Pass holders, and what are the employer's medical obligations for EP holders?
expected_answer: Buying work injury compensation (WIC) insurance is only mandatory if the employer is employing manual workers or non-manual workers earning less than $1,600 a month. Whether or not insurance has been purchased, the employer is still required to pay compensation for an eligible claim. Separately, providing medical insurance is not a requirement for employing EP holders; most EP holders may already have their own medical insurance or may want to choose their own coverage. For EP holders without existing medical insurance, employers can choose to provide insurance coverage as part of the employment contract or encourage EP holders to get their own. The medical insurance requirement applies only to Work Permit and S Pass holders, in line with employers' existing responsibility for the upkeep and maintenance of their migrant workers, including the provision of medical treatment. As for broader medical obligations, employers are obligated to provide paid sick leave, including dental leave, to any employee covered under the Employment Act. Under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), employers are also obligated to pay any eligible claims for workplace injuries. Finally, if the EP holder is a manual worker, the employer is required to purchase work injury compensation insurance for them.

question: According to the notice on the MOM page about the Long-Term Visit Pass for Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass holders, what action must users take and why, and by what date does this requirement apply?
expected_answer: Users whose browser version will not be supported after 27 May 2018 must either enable the Transport Layer Security (TLS) of their web browser or upgrade to the latest version of their browser, in order to continue transacting with MOM securely.

question: A pass holder who currently holds an Employment Pass wants to switch to an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) and is concerned about the impact on their spouse's existing Work Permit. They also want to update their contact details online to ensure MOM can reach them. What online service should they use to update their contact details, what login method is required, and what concern does MOM's FAQ address regarding the effect of switching from an Employment Pass to a ONE Pass on a spouse's Work Permit? Additionally, if they are using an older browser to access this service, what does MOM advise regarding browser requirements after 27 May 2018?
expected_answer: To update their contact details so MOM can reach them in the future, the pass holder should log in to the Employment Pass eService with their Singpass. MOM's FAQ addresses the concern of whether a spouse will lose their existing Work Permit if the pass holder changes from an Employment Pass to an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass). Additionally, if the pass holder is using an older browser version, MOM advises that it will not be supported after 27 May 2018, and the user should either enable Transport Layer Security (TLS) in their web browser or upgrade to the latest version of their browser in order to continue transacting with MOM securely.

question: What is the name of the government ministry whose logo appears on the page about the COMPASS C5 Skills Bonus - Shortage Occupation List (SOL) for Employment Pass eligibility?
expected_answer: The Ministry of Manpower. Its logo and name appear on the page related to the COMPASS C5 Skills bonus - Shortage Occupation List (SOL), which explains that Employment Pass (EP) candidates filling roles on the SOL can qualify for points under the C5 Skills bonus.
